FINAL FIRST PASS INVENTORY - http://127.0.0.1:5000 - VulnBlazor Application

=== TECHNOLOGY STACK ===
- Server: Kestrel (ASP.NET Core development server)
- Framework: ASP.NET Core (antiforgery cookie present)
- UI: Blazor WebAssembly (blazor-enhanced-nav header, SPA routing)
- Backend API: ServiceStack v10.08 (X-Powered-By: ServiceStack/10.08)
- API Docs: Swagger UI v5.32.6 (/swagger)
- OpenAPI Spec: OpenAPI 3.0.4 at /swagger/v1/swagger.json
- Frontend libs: Vue.js, Tailwind CSS, Highlight.js
- Database: SQLite (inferred from data patterns)
- Environment: Development mode exposed

=== AUTH MECHANISM ===
- Cookie-based authentication (antiforgery cookie set)
- Login: POST /Account/Login (302 redirect for unauthenticated users)
- Register: /Account/Register
- Logout: POST /Account/Logout
- External auth: POST /Account/PerformExternalLogin, POST /Account/Manage/LinkExternalLogin
- Role-based access: Employee, Manager, Admin roles observed

Route pattern: /{format}/{operation} (format: json, xml, html)

1.  POST /json/GetUserId - Get current user ID

=== CLIENT ASSETS ===

=== DATA EXPOSED WITHOUT AUTHENTICATION ===
- Employee identifiers: UUIDs, usernames, first names, last names, display names
- Employee profile URLs and image paths
- Full booking records: room types, room numbers, dates, costs, employee assignments
- Coupon data: discount values, expiry dates, codes

- User directory via /api/QueryUsers and /users/id/{Id}
- Complete API schemas: /swagger/v1/swagger.json, /metadata, /metadata/js
- ServiceStack operation metadata with role requirements exposed

=== PLAYBOOK CANDIDATES (Flagged for Testing) ===

[AUTHORIZATION BYPASS]
- GET query endpoints return all data without authentication (QueryTodos, QueryBookings, QueryUsers, GetUserId, GetUserInfo)
- ServiceStack /json/ endpoints mirror OpenAPI auth bypass
- Role-based endpoints (QueryUsers=Admin, DeleteBooking=Manager) accessible without auth
- /api/QueryUsers exposes full user directory publicly

[STORED XSS]
- Todo text field returns unescaped HTML/script tags in API responses
- Payloads visible in /api/QueryTodos and /todos responses
- Blazor rendering of untrusted todo content

[INFORMATION DISCLOSURE]
- Swagger UI publicly accessible at /swagger with full API documentation
- ServiceStack metadata at /metadata exposes operation names, parameters, and role requirements
- /metadata/js exposes JavaScript client generation metadata
- Development environment running with debug features
- User profile images publicly accessible at /img/profiles/

[ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT]
- /Account/Register allows unauthenticated user registration
- /Account/Manage/DownloadPersonalData endpoint (auth required but worth testing)
- External login integration endpoints exposed

[API ABUSE]
- BatchRequest endpoints available for bulk operations
- No rate limiting observed
- Pagination parameters (Skip, Take) allow data enumeration

input_validation_opens_access.content:
INPUT VALIDATION: PUT /todos/{id}.json OPENS ACCESS on malformed input

DEMONSTRATED Findings:

1. PUT creates on non-existent IDs (should be 404):
   - Request: PUT /todos/99999.json body={"id":99999,"text":"test","isFinished":false}
   - Response: 200 OK with {"id":99999,"text":"test","isFinished":false}
   - Control: PUT /todos/1.json (existing) returns 200 update
   - Impact: Unauthenticated resource creation via PUT; ID space pollution

2. Negative IDs accepted (boundary validation missing):
   - Request: PUT /todos/-1.json body={"id":-1,"text":"test","isFinished":false}
   - Response: 200 OK with {"id":-1,"text":"test","isFinished":false}
   - Impact: No lower bound validation on resource IDs

3. Path ID silently overrides body ID:
   - Request: PUT /todos/2.json body={"id":999,"text":"test","isFinished":false}
   - Response: 200 OK with {"id":2,"text":"test","isFinished":false} (body ID=999 ignored)
   - Impact: Confusing API behavior; potential race conditions

4. Content-Type validation bypassed:
   - Request: POST /api/CreateTodo with Content-Type: text/plain body={"text":"test"}
   - Response: 200 OK with created item
   - Request: POST /api/CreateTodo with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded body=text=test
   - Response: 200 OK with created item
   - Impact: No Content-Type enforcement; potential for alternate parsing attacks

5. Stack trace disclosure in error responses:
   - Request: POST /api/CreateTodo body={"text":12345} (wrong type)
   - Response: 400 with full stack trace including:
     * Internal class: ACorpBlazor.ServiceModel.CreateTodo
     * Framework paths: ServiceStack.Host.Handlers.ServiceStackHandlerBase.cs:line 232
     * Full exception chain with line numbers
   - Control: Well-formed request returns clean JSON
   - Impact: Information disclosure aiding further attacks

UNVERIFIED: Whether non-existent ID creation bypasses any authorization that might exist for authenticated endpoints.

weaknesses.description: PUT creates new resources instead of updating existing ones; non-existent IDs return 200 and create items. Negative IDs accepted (-1). Stack trace disclosure in JSON error responses exposes internal class names, file paths, and framework details. DEMONSTRATED: Wrong type in POST /api/CreateTodo returns full System.Text.Json.JsonException stack trace with ACorpBlazor.ServiceModel.CreateTodo, ServiceStack internal paths, and line numbers.
